about: What Bread Planner shows for each input, recorded from the code before the rebuild and reproduced by every step since. Step 3c left out the hidden manual-rye recipe, which the rebuild does not carry, from the saved-data results. tests/baseline/baseline.test.ts checks the current code against it.
recordedFrom: src/ as in commit 3bc6ca2, with uncommitted changes
texts: Keep an established starter on its regular feeding routine.
Mix 14 g mature starter, 35.5 g Anita's all-purpose flour, 35.5 g whole-wheat flour and 71 g water. Keep it separate from the autolyse and cover. You use 100 g in the dough and keep 56 g.
Use when aerated and puffy, and a spoonful floats in room-temperature water. If it sinks, allow more fermentation before mixing.
Mix Anita's all-purpose flour (400 g), whole-wheat flour (50 g), water (340 g). Cover. Keep the remaining ingredients for the final mix.
Add rye flour (50 g), leaven used (100 g), salt (10 g), water (50 g) after the autolyse. Mix until incorporated.
Keep covered in a warm place, about 75°F to 80°F / 24°C to 27°C.
With wet hands, stretch and fold all four sides vigorously, then go around a second time. These early turns build the gluten structure.
Vigorously again: stretch and fold all four sides twice, with wet hands.
From here, one round: stretch and fold all four sides once, with wet hands.
Stretch and fold all four sides once, with wet hands.
Turn the dough out of its container onto your work surface. Cut it into equal pieces and shape each into a taut round.
Look for a billowy dough and 20% to 30% volume increase.
Cover the rounds. Prepare towel-lined baskets dusted with rice flour.
Fold the edges toward the center and roll into a taut round. Place it seam-side up in a prepared basket.
Leave the baskets covered at room temperature.
Cover the shaped loaves in their baskets and refrigerate overnight.
Take the loaf out of the fridge
Allow the loaf to warm while the oven and pots heat.
Place the lidded Dutch oven or pots in the oven and heat to 540°F / 282°C. Use one suitable pot per loaf baked at once.
Dust the loaf tops. Carefully turn seam-side down into the hot pot, score with a lame or razor, and cover. Reduce oven to 460°F / 238°C.
Remove lid carefully: hot steam can escape. Continue at 460°F / 238°C.
Bake until the crust is a rich golden brown; extend the uncovered bake if needed.
Transfer to a wire rack. The base should sound hollow when tapped. Cool each loaf at least 15 minutes before slicing.
The loaf is ready to slice.
Mix 28 g mature starter, 71 g Anita's all-purpose flour, 71 g whole-wheat flour and 142 g water. Keep it separate from the autolyse and cover. You use 200 g in the dough and keep 112 g.
Mix Anita's all-purpose flour (800 g), whole-wheat flour (100 g), water (680 g). Cover. Keep the remaining ingredients for the final mix.
Add rye flour (100 g), leaven used (200 g), salt (20 g), water (100 g) after the autolyse. Mix until incorporated.
Cover the shaped loaves in their baskets and refrigerate overnight. Keep later batches chilled until their own warm-up.
Allow the first batch to warm while the oven and pots heat.
Remove only this batch from the refrigerator. Later loaves have a longer cold proof.
Bring the dough back to room temperature before its own bake.
Clean the pot, replace its lid and return the oven to 540°F / 282°C. Load the next batch once the pot and oven are hot.
This batch is ready to slice.
All loaves out of the oven
Take both loaves out of the fridge
Allow the loaves to warm while the oven and pots heat.
The loaves are ready to slice.
Mix 42 g mature starter, 106.5 g Anita's all-purpose flour, 106.5 g whole-wheat flour and 213 g water. Keep it separate from the autolyse and cover. You use 300 g in the dough and keep 168 g.
Mix Anita's all-purpose flour (1200 g), whole-wheat flour (150 g), water (1020 g). Cover. Keep the remaining ingredients for the final mix.
Add rye flour (150 g), leaven used (300 g), salt (30 g), water (150 g) after the autolyse. Mix until incorporated.
Mix 7.5 g (about 1 tbsp) of mature starter with 100 g water, then add 50 g white-bread flour and 50 g whole-wheat flour. Cover at room temperature. You use 100 g in the dough and keep 107.5 g.
Disperse the leaven used in the initial water, about 80°F / 27°C. Add white and whole-wheat flour; mix until no dry flour remains. Cover for 25 to 40 minutes.
Work in the salt and reserved water. Keep mixing if the dough separates; it should come together again.
Cover and keep at 75°F to 80°F / 24°C to 27°C.
Wet your hand. Stretch one quadrant over the dough; rotate and repeat to fold all four sides.
Repeat the four-sided stretch and fold, with wet hands.
Dust the top, divide equally and turn flour-side down. Shape taut rounds with the dusting flour on the outside.
Look for a billowy dough and 20% to 30% volume increase. The book allows up to one more hour with folds if needed; wait until the dough is ready before moving on.
Cover the rounds for 30 minutes. Line proofing baskets or bowls with towels and generously dust with rice flour.
Turn flour-side down. Stretch and fold the bottom, sides and top over the center; roll seam-side down into a taut round. Place seam-side up in a prepared basket.
Cover the baskets and refrigerate for 10 to 12 hours.
Warm the loaf to room temperature
Remove the loaf from the refrigerator.
Bring the dough back to room temperature before baking; use its condition, rather than the clock alone.
Place the lidded Dutch oven or pots in the oven and heat to 500°F / 260°C. Use one suitable pot per loaf baked at once.
Dust the loaf tops. Carefully turn seam-side down into the hot pot, score with a lame or razor, and cover. Reduce oven to 450°F / 232°C.
Remove lid carefully: hot steam can escape. Continue at 450°F / 232°C.
Cover and keep at 75°F to 80°F / 24°C to 27°C for 3 to 4 hours.
Mix 15 g (about 1 tbsp) of mature starter with 200 g water, then add 100 g white-bread flour and 100 g whole-wheat flour. Cover at room temperature. You use 200 g in the dough and keep 215 g.
Cover the baskets and refrigerate for 10 to 12 hours. Keep later batches chilled until their own warm-up.
Remove only the loaves in the first batch.
Clean the pot, replace its lid and return the oven to 500°F / 260°C. Load the next batch once the pot and oven are hot.
Warm both loaves to room temperature
Remove the loaves from the refrigerator.
Mix 22.5 g (about 1 tbsp) of mature starter with 300 g water, then add 150 g white-bread flour and 150 g whole-wheat flour. Cover at room temperature. You use 300 g in the dough and keep 322.5 g.
Mix 56 g mature starter, 142 g Anita's all-purpose flour, 142 g whole-wheat flour and 284 g water. Keep it separate from the autolyse and cover. You use 400 g in the dough and keep 224 g.

Mix 70 g mature starter, 177.5 g Anita's all-purpose flour, 177.5 g whole-wheat flour and 355 g water. Keep it separate from the autolyse and cover. You use 500 g in the dough and keep 280 g.

Add rye flour (400 g), leaven used (800 g), salt (80 g), water (400 g) after the autolyse. Mix until incorporated.
Mix 30 g (about 1 tbsp) of mature starter with 400 g water, then add 200 g white-bread flour and 200 g whole-wheat flour. Cover at room temperature. You use 400 g in the dough and keep 430 g.
Mix 37.5 g (about 1 tbsp) of mature starter with 500 g water, then add 250 g white-bread flour and 250 g whole-wheat flour. Cover at room temperature. You use 500 g in the dough and keep 537.5 g.
Mix 60 g (about 1 tbsp) of mature starter with 800 g water, then add 400 g white-bread flour and 400 g whole-wheat flour. Cover at room temperature. You use 800 g in the dough and keep 860 g.

Mix 0 g mature starter, 0 g Anita's all-purpose flour, 0 g whole-wheat flour and 0 g water. Keep it separate from the autolyse and cover. This makes 200 g less than the 200 g the dough needs; increase the build.
Mix 27.3 g mature starter, 69.1 g Anita's all-purpose flour, 69.1 g whole-wheat flour and 138.2 g water. Keep it separate from the autolyse and cover. You use 194.6 g in the dough and keep 109 g.
Mix Anita's all-purpose flour (778.6 g), whole-wheat flour (97.3 g), water (708.5 g). Cover. Keep the remaining ingredients for the final mix.
